question: Razorpay SDE-1, hiring-manager round (about 1.5 hours, with technical and behavioral parts). Reported "common but tricky" questions: **Why Razorpay? Why are you leaving your current organisation, and especially, why leave a big organisation to join Razorpay? What would you do if you got a better offer than this one? What does work-life balance mean to you?** The same round also asked about past failure and about convincing a team lead on a trade-off.
lookingFor: Genuine, researched motivation for the company, not flattery.
A forward-looking reason for changing jobs, without criticising the current employer.
Honesty and consistency on commitment and the better-offer question.
Realistic expectations about workload and boundaries.
Self-awareness: what environment you thrive in.
answer:
These are character and motivation questions. Prepare honest answers in your own words; interviewers detect rehearsed lines.

**Why Razorpay.** Research the company: it is an Indian payments and fintech company (payment gateway and related financial products). Choose two or three reasons you can support: working on payments where correctness and reliability are critical, high-scale transaction systems, a product used by many businesses, a team or tech stack that matches your skills, learning opportunity and ownership at a faster-growing company. Connect it to evidence: a project, an API you used, or a concept you studied. Avoid "good brand" or "good salary" as a main reason.

**Why leave your current (or a bigger) organisation.** Talk about what you are moving *toward*: more ownership, closer exposure to customers and production, faster learning, a domain you care about. Be positive about your current place ("I learned X there"). Never criticise colleagues or management. For a fresher, say what you want from a first role and why this one fits. Big-organisation answer: you value broader scope and a visible impact over a narrow role.

**What would you do if you got a better offer.** Be honest and calm: you have chosen this company for specific reasons (the work, team, growth), compensation is one factor but not the only one, and if you accept an offer you honour it. Do not say money does not matter at all, and do not make threats or promises you cannot keep. If you have competing offers, say you are evaluating on role, team and learning.

**Work-life balance.** Define it as sustainable performance: focused work, clear priorities, flexibility for urgent releases or incidents, and the ability to recharge. Show you can commit during critical times and protect time to learn and rest otherwise. Do not say you will work any hours, and do not say you want no pressure.

**Mistakes to avoid.** Generic answers that fit any company; contradicting what you said to the recruiter; badmouthing; inventing facts about the company; and having no questions for the manager. Ask about team ownership, on-call and how the team measures success.
followUps: What do you know about our products, and which would you improve?
Where do you see yourself in three years?
Tell me about a time you failed and what you learned.
Tell me about a time you convinced your lead about a technical trade-off.
